description: A mathematically-inclined junior who excels in theoretical computer science and algorithm design but has only worked in high-level languages like Java and Python.

nodes.personalizationRationale: As the student has no_prior_exposure to C, this node provides the necessary language foundation for OS development.
nodes.title: C Programming Fundamentals for Systems
nodes.description: A primer on C syntax, pointers, and memory management specifically for students with no prior systems programming experience.

nodes.title: Foundational Computer Architecture Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: Bridges the gap between hardware and software for a student with no_prior_exposure to low-level concepts.
nodes.description: A review of CPU registers, the fetch-decode-execute cycle, and basic computer architecture to contextualize OS operations.
Guided walkthrough of using the Linux command line and development environment used in the course projects.
nodes.title: Navigating the OS Development Environment
nodes.personalizationRationale: Provides essential environment setup support for a student starting with no_prior_exposure to OS toolchains.

nodes.description: Exploring the architecture of the kernel, including the distinction between user mode and kernel mode and the role of system calls.
nodes.title: OS Services and System Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory core content for all students covering the structural design of operating systems.
Foundational process management theory required for all cumulative exam material.
nodes.title: Process Lifecycle and Management
nodes.description: Defining the process abstraction, the Process Control Block (PCB), and the state transition diagram.
Methods for processes to communicate, focusing on shared memory mechanisms and message passing protocols.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement to understand how isolated processes interact safely in a system.
nodes.title: Inter-Process Communication (IPC)

nodes.description: Introduction to multi-threaded programming, threading libraries (Pthreads), and the benefits of concurrency.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core content for understanding how modern OSs handle multiple flows of execution.
nodes.title: Threading Models and Libraries

nodes.description: Evaluation of CPU scheduling algorithms including FCFS, SJF, and Round Robin using performance metrics.
nodes.title: CPU Scheduling Criteria and Algorithms
nodes.personalizationRationale: Critical core topic for modeling system performance and resource allocation.
Mandatory midterm checkpoint to ensure mastery of foundational concepts before the exam.
nodes.title: Midterm Review: Foundations and Processes
nodes.description: A comprehensive review and practice assessment covering all material from Chapters 1-5 to prepare for the midterm.

nodes.title: Synchronization Primitives and Mutexes
nodes.personalizationRationale: Essential core module for building thread-safe OS primitives and applications.
nodes.description: Solving the critical section problem using hardware and software solutions like mutex locks and semaphores.
Application of synchronization primitives to classic problems like the Producer-Consumer and Dining Philosophers.
nodes.title: Classic Problems of Synchronization
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement focused on practical application of synchronization theory.

nodes.title: Deadlock Characterization and Avoidance
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement to understand resource allocation safety and deadlock detection.
nodes.description: Identifying deadlock conditions and implementing Banker's algorithm for deadlock avoidance.

nodes.title: Physical Memory and Paging Structures
nodes.personalizationRationale: Fundamental memory management concepts required for the final project and exam.
nodes.description: Principles of contiguous allocation, fragmentation, and the implementation of paging and page tables.

nodes.title: Virtual Memory and Page Replacement
nodes.personalizationRationale: Core requirement focusing on virtualizing memory to support larger applications.
nodes.description: Advanced memory concepts including demand paging, thrashing, and page replacement algorithms (LRU, FIFO).
Overview of the I/O subsystem architecture, including interrupt-driven I/O and DMA performance tradeoffs.
nodes.personalizationRationale: Mandatory core material regarding the OS interface with external hardware.
nodes.title: I/O Systems and Performance

nodes.description: Implementation details of file systems, including disk block allocation and metadata management.
nodes.title: File System Implementation Strategies
nodes.personalizationRationale: Required capstone content for understanding persistent storage implementations.

nodes.title: Final Cumulative Course Review
nodes.personalizationRationale: Final assessment checkpoint for the cumulative final exam covering all blocks.
nodes.description: A cumulative review of the entire syllabus, focusing on cross-topic connections between memory, scheduling, and sync.
